items.message: This change implements GATE-REVIEW-9: separating which lenses a repository *has* from which lenses *gate* a pull request. The core mechanism is a `gating` parameter on `review_workflows.register()`, resolved at run time against the bound adapter rather than at registration, and deliberately excluded from the registered callable's signature to prevent it appearing as a `--arg`. The documentation, gates table, objectives table, and tests all land consistently. The intent matches the implementation…[truncated]
Ordering of gating lenses follows adapter declaration order, but the comment says so without a test in the implementation path itself.
`__qualname__` left as closure's own is asserted in prose but not in the test suite.

This change adds a `gating` parameter to `review_workflows.register()`, separating which lenses a repository *has* from which lenses *gate* a pull request. The implementation is documentation, design docs, a module-level function, and tests — no data structures that grow with usage, no loops over external state, no network calls introduced on any hot path. The fan-out in `review_all_lenses` was already bounded by the number of declared lenses; filtering that set to a named subset makes it strict…[truncated]

This change introduces a `gating` parameter to `review_workflows.register()`, allowing a repository to declare which bound lenses gate a pull request independently of which lenses exist. The security-relevant surface is narrow: the new code validates the `gating` collection against the adapter's declared lenses at run time, refuses an empty selection explicitly, and deliberately excludes the `gating` parameter from the registered callable's introspectable signature to prevent it from becoming a …[truncated]

This change adds `GATE-REVIEW-9`: a `gating=` parameter on `review_workflows.register()` that decouples which lenses exist from which lenses gate a pull request. The implementation is in `review.py`, documented in `docs/extending.md` and `design/gates.md`, and the tests in `test_enforced_review.py` cover the new behaviour with notable care. I examined whether each behaviour the description promises is named by a test, whether the assertions would survive reverting the change, and whether the clo…[truncated]
No test asserts the `gating_unknown` refusal message when multiple unknown lenses are named simultaneously.
The `gating_empty` refusal is not asserted to exit with `Status.BLOCKED` in a way that would distinguish it from `Status.FAILED`.
